claim_dispositions.claim: The RV feature units must support the proposed square-root-of-horizon normalization.
claim_dispositions.evidence: tools/deriv_dataset.py lines 94 and 102: r1 = lc.diff() is the log-close change of one one-minute bar and rv_w = r1.rolling(w, min_periods=max(5, w // 3)).std(), so rv_w is a per-minute standard deviation in log-return units and ret_w / (sqrt(w) * rv_60m) is dimensionless. The dataset's own stretch_w (line 109) already divides by r1.rolling(w).std() * np.sqrt(w). ret_w is a wall-clock return and rv_w counts bars; they agree where bars are contiguous (99.984% of EURUSD development bars).
claim_dispositions.consequence: A-056 can use the normalization as written. It must not use the 1440-bar scale on Mondays without the R6-GAP-01 correction.

claim_dispositions.claim: The installed CatBoost Ordered configuration must honor the intended chronological history.
claim_dispositions.evidence: Lab test x-r6-libcheck (discovery/round6/checks/library_behaviour_fixture.py and .log), CatBoost 1.2.10: Ordered with has_time=True resolves to permutation_count=1, without it to 4. With all other randomness off, two seeds give identical test probabilities with has_time=True (largest difference 0) and differ by up to 4.99e-02 without it. Reversing the row order changes the Ordered has_time model by up to 1.22e-01 and a Plain model by 2.2e-16.
claim_dispositions.consequence: A-032 must pass rows sorted by decision time and set has_time=True; the default Ordered mode draws four random permutations and is not chronological. Label overlap between neighbouring rows is not handled by the library, so the H-non-overlapping fit origins in the specification are required.

claim_dispositions.claim: Standalone ensemble producers may differ in weight handling, truncation and numerical backend.
claim_dispositions.evidence: tools/cpcv_deriv_x.py (0.10) lines 285-331. Weights: the LightGBM member is fitted with sample_weight when weights are set (line 289); the XGBoost fit (line 322, g.fit(Xf, yf, eval_set=[(Xv, yv)], verbose=False)) and the CatBoost fit (line 329) receive none. Missing values: CatBoost gets NaN replaced by -999.0 (line 325), the other two get NaN. Truncation: each member stops on its own validation AUC with patience 80; x-r6-libcheck shows XGBoost 3.2.0 predicts with the first best_iteration + 1 trees after early stopping and CatBoost resolves use_best_model=True and keeps best_iteration + 1 trees. Backend: XGBoost tree_method='hist' and CatBoost both run on the CPU; CatBoost's CPU defaults resolved to Plain boosting, MVS bootstrap and 254 borders, while A-075 specifies 128 borders and a Bayesian bootstrap on the GPU. b1bench measured the CUDA XGBoost model as a different model: on its one benchmark path [USDJPY·15m] the predictions and the path AUC differ from the CPU model's (results/json/deriv_b1bench_compute_result.json, block D_gpu_gbm; a compute benchmark, not a result of record).
claim_dispositions.consequence: The GPU producers of A-075 are new recipes, compared with the CPU members within a tolerance and never bit for bit. Weights go to all three members or to none; the queued e31ens3 uses no weights, so its members are consistent with each other.

own_gaps.title: Contract types that pay on move size: durations, prices and realized frequencies
own_gaps.prior_why: Move size is predictable on this feed and direction is not: the magnitude gate's test AUC is 0.640 to 0.707 by pair (path means; results/json/deriv_e13mag50_<PAIR>_15m_result.json, mag_gate.mag_auc_test) against 0.498 to 0.526 for direction. The venue lists touch, no-touch, ends-between, ends-outside, stays-between and goes-outside contracts for frxUSDJPY (results/json/deriv_api_probe_result.json, contracts_for, 2026-07-02). The venue prices volatility itself, so the comparison that matters is the model's probability against the quoted price, not against the base rate; the prior stays low until quotes are on disk. Which types exist at durations of one day or less is not recorded.
own_gaps.mechanism: Volatility clusters and follows the clock and the calendar, so the probability that price touches a barrier or ends inside a range within H minutes is forecastable. A venue quote that conditions on a slower or coarser volatility estimate than the model would leave a margin on some contracts.
own_gaps.spec: Step 1, one read-only metadata call per pair: contracts_for with every type's minimum and maximum duration and barrier rules. Step 2, only if a size-paying type has a duration of one day or less: sample proposals on a fixed grid of pair, UTC hour, duration and barrier distance in units of trailing realized volatility, for two or more weeks, storing ask price and payout; implied probability is ask divided by payout. Step 3, no venue contact: compute the realized touch and range frequencies for the same grid from development ticks, fit the existing magnitude heads (HAR and LightGBM) to those outcomes inside the CPCV folds, and compare the model's probability with the quoted implied probability. Step 4: a key would be (pair, contract type, duration); the owner defines its breakeven and certification rule, because the payout varies by quote.
own_gaps.nearest_existing: e13mag50 and e62har use magnitude only as a gate on direction trades. B-002 reconciles Rise/Fall payouts and settlement only. No cluster trades a contract that pays on move size.
own_gaps.fast_kill_falsifier: Stop after step 1 if no size-paying type has a duration of one day or less. Stop after step 3 if no decile of (model probability minus quoted probability) has a realized frequency above the quote by more than the venue's margin.
own_gaps.cost: Build M. Steps 1 and 2: venue metadata and proposal calls, 0 model fits. Step 3: 20 to 40 magnitude fits per pair.

own_gaps.title: London and Asian decision sessions as separate keys
own_gaps.prior_why: Every stored run decides inside New York hours: session values ny 517, nylate 9, nypm 7, nyeve 7, nyam 7 (08:00-17:00, 13:00-22:00, 13:00-17:00, 17:00-22:00, 08:00-13:00 New York time; cpcv_deriv_x.py LOCAL_WINDOWS). The harness already accepts --session ldn (08:00-16:00 London) and asia (09:00-18:00 Tokyo) from scripts/sessions.py. The feed is continuous on business days (EURUSD: 99.98% of minute bars follow the previous one by 60 s). These hours are outcomes that no run has scored, so they add evidence instead of re-mining New York rows; whether they hold more signal is unknown, and each new key adds to the multiple-testing count. The goal fixes New York 08:00-17:00, so this is a change of certification scope.
own_gaps.mechanism: Each pair's home session has its own flow and fixing structure (Tokyo fix, London open, ECB and London fixes). One recorded quote outside New York hours paid 1.90 (breakeven 0.526) against 1.77 and 1.52 to 1.67 inside them, so the venue breakeven may also differ by session.
own_gaps.spec: H = 15. For each pair run the default LightGBM (e1t recipe) and the kernel model (e30nystroem recipe) with --session ldn and --session asia, fit session equal to the evaluation session, coverages 0.03, 0.05 and 0.10, all 15 paths and 4 forward folds, tradeable-only rows. Check the venue's purchase restrictions for those hours first (contracts_for trading times). Keys are (pair, 15m, side, session). No feature or model search before these baselines are read.

own_gaps.fast_kill_falsifier: Kill a session for a pair if neither model has a side with 12 counted paths and a mean path win rate of at least 0.541; a side that passes goes to the sign-null replay and the drift placebo before anything else is tried on it.
own_gaps.cost: No build. 28 runs of 19 fits: one to one and a half hours one fit at a time, about 45 minutes with parallel paths, which wait for program decision 7 (from the run times of the two recipes in checks/harness_regression_011b.log; estimates, since the rows differ by session).

own_gaps.title: One registered forward look on data collected after the development window
own_gaps.prior_why: After more than 540 stored runs on one development year a new development pass is weak evidence whatever the model. Data collected after 2026-07-31 has been opened only by the registered USDJPY look. At the operating coverage a path holds a median of 59 trades, so a single key cannot be confirmed on three to seven forward months; a frozen basket of keys can.
own_gaps.mechanism: Frozen configurations scored once on outcomes that no selection step has seen are free of the search-wide selection bias. Pooling a fixed list of keys trades per-key resolution for the trade count that a one-sided test of 0.541 needs.
own_gaps.spec: Freeze a list of at most 12 non-USDJPY key-configurations by a rule written before the look (for example each key's best VALID run by paths clear, then p10). Refit each once on the whole development window. Score post-development rows once, tradeable-only, ties lose, first-come de-overlap. Primary statistic: the basket's pooled win rate against 0.541, one-sided alpha 0.025, with a day-block bootstrap; secondary: per-key rates, reported and not tested. Register the look date and the list in the lab log first. A basket pass certifies nothing per key: it decides whether per-key confirmation is worth a second look.
own_gaps.nearest_existing: The two-look USDJPY procedure (holdout/run_look1.sh). E-010 computes power; no cluster registers a forward look for the other keys.
own_gaps.fast_kill_falsifier: Do not open the data if the power calculation (E-010) gives less than 50% power for a true basket rate of 0.57. If the look is taken and the basket's lower bound is below 0.541, the listed keys stay DO NOT DEPLOY and are not re-selected on that data.
own_gaps.cost: Build S (holdout_eval.py exists). 12 refits and one scoring pass.

row_notes.D-033: Two parts change on the evaluated path with outcomes that have matured there: the 60-session residual archive of the third forecast and the optional daily updates. That is the continuing-policy question of program decision 13 (stage 13 holds D-023 and D-024 for it), so those parts wait for decision 13 as well. The two fit-fixed forecasts and their equal-weight pool wait for decision 8 only.
row_notes.D-035: The trailing 20-day and half-life empirical distributions are updated with matured outcomes of the evaluated path (the specification: archives are updated only with matured outcomes). That is the continuing-policy question of program decision 13, so those arms wait for decision 13 as well. The fixed t5 arm waits for decision 8 only.
row_notes.D-036: The recursive-least-squares arm updates the coefficients on the evaluated path with targets that have matured there. That is the continuing-policy question of program decision 13, so that arm waits for decision 13 as well. The static-coefficient arms wait for decision 8 only.
row_notes.E-009: The specification leaves the refit-null requirement to E-030 (stage 14), which runs only after a raw survivor and waits for program decision 13. This test does not need it: it computes its joint inference on cached forecasts and labels that inference as conditional. A promotion needs both.
row_notes.E-012: The specification starts after the settlement contract is verified. In stage 3 that is the development-data audit of E-007 (stage 1): the replay compares entry and exit prices with the stored labels under the dataset's own convention (scripts/deriv_dataset.py, settle; proposal R6-L-02 says to reuse it and to add a development-only report) and makes no venue call. Whether the venue settles contracts that way is B-002 (stage 7) and waits for program decision 9.
row_notes.D-050: The specification starts from the residuals of D-035. It needs that test's fit-side part only: standardized residuals of out-of-fold predictions, with the tails fitted on fit exceedances (proposal R6-M2-24). The empirical distributions of D-035 that are updated on the evaluated path wait for program decision 13 and are not used here.
